subproblem.title: A.e. finiteness of liminf of slice-mass majorants on all balls (V4(ii), step 7)
subproblem.statement: Assume (MM), the exact frozen third conjunct of the sibling theorem cbr_measure_convergence_tools: for all P ∈ ℕ, Borel measures μ_j on ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ), continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for all j and Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P ∈ ℕ, μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) Borel measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ → [0, ∞], (i, k, t) ↦ Z_{i,k}(t). Suppose that sup_i μ_i(B_{k+1}(0)) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ, and that Z_{i,k}(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_i(B_{k+1}(0) ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all i, k ∈ ℕ and all t ∈ ℝ. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, liminf_{i→∞} Z_{i,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (G : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ j, μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}) < ∞) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (t : ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → Z j t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs j (G ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), t ∈ Ioo a b → liminf (fun j => Z j t) atTop ≤ g t) ∧ ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun j => μs j (G ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b})) atTop) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (Z : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Continuous f → (∀ k : ℕ, ⨆ i, μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1)) < ∞) → (∀ (i k : ℕ) (t : ℝ), Z i k t ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μs i (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1) ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ k : ℕ, liminf (fun i => Z i k t) atTop < ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Write W_k := B_{k+1}(0) and Λ_k := sup_i μ_i(W_k), which is < ∞ by hypothesis.

1. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ. Apply (MM) with P, the measures μ_j, the continuous f, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m), L and Z_j(t) := Z_{j,k}(t). Its hypotheses hold: μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ μ_j(W_k) ≤ Λ_k < ∞ (measure_mono, le_iSup); and the majorant inequality Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_j(W_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) holds for every t, in particular for t ∈ (−m, m). (MM) yields a measurable g = g_{k,m} : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (α) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t); and (β) ∫_{(−m,m)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}).

2. The right side of (β) is finite: every term μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) is ≤ Λ_k, so liminf_j μ_j(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ Λ_k < ∞ (Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'), and L < ∞, so the product is < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top). Hence the lower integral of the measurable function g with respect to L¹ restricted to (−m, m) is finite, so g(t) < ∞ for a.e. t with respect to that restricted measure (MeasureTheory.ae_lt_top), i.e. (ae_restrict_iff' with measurableSet_Ioo) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞.

3. Combining (α) with step 2 (the intersection of two full-measure sets has full measure): for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.

4. Fix k. A countable intersection of full-measure sets has full measure (ae_all_iff over m ∈ ℕ): for L¹-a.e. t, for every m ∈ ℕ, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. For such t choose m ∈ ℕ with m > |t| (exists_nat_gt); then −m < t < m, so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. Thus for every k: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞.

5. Applying ae_all_iff once more, now over k ∈ ℕ: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each k, m apply (MM) with G := B_{k+1}(0) and (a, b) := (−m, m); finiteness from sup_i μ_i(B_{k+1}(0)) < ∞.
The bound ∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L Λ_k < ∞ makes the measurable majorant g a.e. finite on (−m, m), so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m).
Countable intersection over m (the intervals (−m, m) cover ℝ) and then over k gives the a.e. statement for all k.

subproblem.title: IM closure in ℝ^P from local liminf mass bounds (V4(ii), steps 9–11)
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ and assume CL(d): for all P ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and currents T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (j ∈ ℕ) such that every T_j is integer multiplicity (IM), sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U, and T_j ⇀ T in U, the current T is IM. Assume (LOC), the exact conclusion of the sibling theorem cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (its hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) are discharged by the parent): for all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and every X ∈ 𝒟_k(U), (1) if M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W with closure(W) compact and contained in U, and every x ∈ U has r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U such that the domain restriction X|_{B_r(x)} = X.restrictDomain ∈ 𝒟_k(B_r(x)) is IM, then X is IM; (2) for every open V ⊆ U, if X is IM then X|_V ∈ 𝒟_k(V) is IM. Let P ∈ ℕ and Z_i, Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ) with every Z_i IM and Z_i ⇀ Z in ℝ^P. Suppose that for every k ∈ ℕ, with W_k := B_{k+1}(0) (open ball), liminf_{i→∞} (M_{W_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, W_k)) < ∞ in [0, ∞], where boundaryMassOn(Y, W) := M_W(∂Y) if d ≥ 1 and := 0 if d = 0. Then Z is IM.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ d : ℕ, (∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U d) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U d), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + boundaryMassOn (Ts j) W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T) → (∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsOpen U → ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → X.massOn W < ∞) → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∃ h : ball x r ⊆ U, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X) ∧ (∀ (V : Set (Euclid P)) (h : V ⊆ U), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h))) → ∀ (P : ℕ) (Zs : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d), (∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Zs i)) → WeaklyConvergesOn Zs Z → (∀ k : ℕ, liminf (fun i => (Zs i).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1)) + boundaryMassOn (Zs i) (ball (0 : Euclid P) ((k : ℝ) + 1))) atTop < ∞) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. For V ⊆ U and T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), T|_V := T.restrictDomain ∈ 𝒟_n(V) is given by T|_V(ω) = T(ω~), where ω~ := testFormOnInclusion(ω) ∈ 𝒟^n(U) is ω regarded as a test form in U (the same underlying differential form). W_k := B_{k+1}(0), which is open, and u_{i,k} := M_{W_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, W_k) ∈ [0, ∞]. By hypothesis liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞ for every k.

1. Bounded subsequences. Fix k ∈ ℕ. Since [0, ∞] is densely ordered and liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞, choose C_k with liminf_i u_{i,k} < C_k < ∞ (exists_between). By Mathlib Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt (its coboundedness side condition holds automatically in the complete lattice [0, ∞]), u_{i,k} < C_k for frequently many i in atTop, so by Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop there is a strictly increasing ψ_k : ℕ → ℕ with u_{ψ_k(l),k} ≤ C_k for every l. Since ψ_k(l) → ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop), for every test form ω the real sequence Z_{ψ_k(l)}(ω) is a subsequence of Z_i(ω) → Z(ω), so Z_{ψ_k(l)} ⇀ Z in ℝ^P as l → ∞.

2. Facts on domain restriction. Let V ⊆ U, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and W ⊆ ℝ^P.
(a) M_W(T|_V) ≤ M_W(T). M_W(T|_V) is the supremum of ofReal(T|_V(ω)) over the admissible ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V), i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (SimonGMT massAdmissibleOn). For such ω, ω~ has the same underlying form, hence is admissible for M_W(T), and T|_V(ω) = T(ω~); so ofReal(T|_V(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) by GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, and sSup_le gives the claim.
(b) If n = n' + 1 then (T|_V).boundary = (T.boundary)|_V. For η ∈ 𝒟^{n'}(V): (T|_V).boundary(η) = T|_V(dη) = T((dη)~) and (T.boundary)|_V(η) = T.boundary(η~) = T(d(η~)). The test forms (dη)~ and d(η~) in 𝒟^{n'+1}(U) have the same underlying form (the exterior derivative of the form underlying η), so they are equal (Subtype.ext), and currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
(c) boundaryMassOn(T|_V, W) ≤ boundaryMassOn(T, W): for n = 0 both sides are 0 by definition; for n = n' + 1, boundaryMassOn(T|_V, W) = M_W((T|_V).boundary) = M_W((T.boundary)|_V) ≤ M_W(T.boundary) = boundaryMassOn(T, W) by (b) and (a).
(d) W ↦ boundaryMassOn(T, W) is monotone: it is identically 0 for n = 0 and equals W ↦ M_W(T.boundary) for n = n' + 1, which is monotone (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono).
(e) If V' ⊆ V ⊆ U then (T|_V)|_{V'} = T|_{V'}: both send ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V') to T evaluated at test forms with the same underlying form ω (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

3. Z is IM in every W_k. Fix k and put Y_l := (Z_{ψ_k(l)})|_{W_k} ∈ 𝒟_d(W_k) and Y := Z|_{W_k} ∈ 𝒟_d(W_k).
(i) Every Y_l is IM by (LOC)(2) applied with U := ℝ^P (open), V := W_k (open) and X := Z_{ψ_k(l)} (IM by hypothesis).
(ii) Y_l ⇀ Y in W_k: for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(W_k), Y_l(ω) = Z_{ψ_k(l)}(ω~) → Z(ω~) = Y(ω) by step 1.
(iii) Let W'' be open with closure(W'') compact and closure(W'') ⊆ W_k; then W'' ⊆ closure(W'') ⊆ W_k. For every l, by 2(a), monotonicity of mass in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono), 2(c) and 2(d): M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'') ≤ M_{W''}(Z_{ψ_k(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ_k(l)}, W'') ≤ M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ_k(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ_k(l)}, W_k) = u_{ψ_k(l),k} ≤ C_k. Hence sup_l (M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'')) ≤ C_k < ∞ (iSup_le).
By CL(d) applied with this P, U := W_k (open), T_l := Y_l and T := Y, the current Z|_{W_k} is IM.

4. Z has locally finite mass in ℝ^P. Let W be open with closure(W) compact (and contained in ℝ^P). A compact set is bounded, so closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) for some r ∈ ℝ (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball); choose k ∈ ℕ with k > r (exists_nat_gt). Then W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) ⊆ W_k (Metric.ball_subset_ball, r ≤ k + 1). By lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) applied to Z_{ψ_k(l)} ⇀ Z (step 1): M_W(Z) ≤ liminf_l M_W(Z_{ψ_k(l)}). For every l, M_W(Z_{ψ_k(l)}) ≤ M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ_k(l)}) ≤ u_{ψ_k(l),k} ≤ C_k, so liminf_l M_W(Z_{ψ_k(l)}) ≤ C_k (Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'). Hence M_W(Z) ≤ C_k < ∞.

5. Conclusion. Let x ∈ ℝ^P and choose k ∈ ℕ with k > |x|. Then B_1(x) ⊆ W_k: if |y − x| < 1 then |y| ≤ |y − x| + |x| < 1 + k (Metric.ball_subset_ball', since 1 + dist(x, 0) ≤ k + 1). By step 3, Z|_{W_k} is IM; by (LOC)(2) applied with U := W_k (open), V := B_1(x) (open) and X := Z|_{W_k}, the current (Z|_{W_k})|_{B_1(x)} is IM, and it equals Z|_{B_1(x)} by 2(e). Thus every x ∈ ℝ^P has r := 1 > 0 with B_1(x) ⊆ ℝ^P and Z|_{B_1(x)} IM. Together with step 4, (LOC)(1) applied with U := ℝ^P (open) and X := Z shows that Z is IM. ∎

Domain restriction does not increase mass or boundary mass, commutes with ∂, and composes; boundaryMassOn is monotone in the region.
(LOC)(2) makes the restrictions Z_{ψ_k(l)}|_{W_k} IM; they converge weakly in W_k with bounded mass and boundary mass on every W'' ⊂⊂ W_k, so CL(d) in W_k makes Z|_{W_k} IM.
Lower semicontinuity along ψ_k gives M_W(Z) ≤ C_k < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ W_k.
B_1(x) ⊆ W_k for k > |x|; (LOC)(2) in W_k gives Z|_{B_1(x)} IM, and (LOC)(1) in ℝ^P gives Z IM.

subproblem.title: Slicing a current and its boundary: combined slice mass bound (V4(ii), steps 5, 7 and 9)
subproblem.statement: Assume (SL), the exact frozen statement of the parent's dependency cmc_slice_mass_bounds: for all P, k ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), admissible representations (μ, ξ) of T and (μ', ξ') of ∂T in U (Borel measures finite on compact subsets of U; a.e. strongly measurable fields of (k+1)- resp. k-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for a.e. x; T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ and ∂T(η) = ∫ ξ'(η) dμ' for all test forms in U) and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ', ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η misses {f = t}, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W, and ∫_{(a,b)} M_W(∂A_t − B_t) dt ≤ L μ(W ∩ {a < f < b}) for open W. Let P, d ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), (μ, ξ) an admissible representation of X and (μ', ξ') an admissible representation of ∂X in U (as above), and f : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0). Then there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all t ∈ ℝ and all test forms ω, η in U, such that for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P and every t ∈ ℝ, with Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t, M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0, h>0} ofReal(h⁻¹) · (μ + μ')(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) in [0, ∞], where boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = M_W(∂Z_t) if d ≥ 1 and = 0 if d = 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:
This is the summed majorant of step 7 of the parent proof (slice mass plus slice-boundary mass); its boundary part absorbs the identity ∂Z_t = −∂B_t of step 9. Fix the data. For a Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, an open W and t ∈ ℝ write J_ν(h) := ofReal(h⁻¹) · ν(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ∈ [0, ∞] and ℓ_ν := liminf_{h → 0+} J_ν(h), the limit inferior along the filter 𝓝[>] 0.

1. First slicing. Apply (SL) with k := d, the open set U, T := X, the representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X, the function f and the constant L (all its hypotheses are hypotheses of the present statement). It yields families A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all t, ω, η; these are the required currents and give the first two conclusions. (SL) also gives M_W(Z_t) ≤ L ℓ_μ for every open W and every t, where Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t. Fix an open W and t ∈ ℝ; it remains to prove the combined bound.

2. Two inequalities in [0, ∞].
(i) For functions u, v with values in [0, ∞] and any filter F: liminf_F u + liminf_F v ≤ liminf_F (u + v). Indeed liminf_F u = sup_{S ∈ F} inf_{x ∈ S} u(x) (Filter.liminf_eq_iSup_iInf), and for S, S' ∈ F we have inf_{x∈S} u(x) + inf_{x∈S'} v(x) ≤ inf_{x ∈ S ∩ S'} (u(x) + v(x)) ≤ liminf_F (u + v), because S ∩ S' ∈ F. In [0, ∞], (sup_{S ∈ F} a_S) + (sup_{S' ∈ F} b_{S'}) ≤ c whenever a_S + b_{S'} ≤ c for all S, S' ∈ F (Mathlib ENNReal.biSup_add_biSup_le'; both index families are nonempty because univ ∈ F), which proves (i).
(ii) J_{μ+μ'}(h) = J_μ(h) + J_{μ'}(h) for every h, by (μ + μ')(E) = μ(E) + μ'(E) (Measure.add_apply) and distributivity. Hence, by (i) with F := 𝓝[>] 0, ℓ_μ + ℓ_{μ'} ≤ ℓ_{μ+μ'}, and multiplying by L (multiplication by a fixed element of [0, ∞] is monotone; mul_add): L ℓ_μ + L ℓ_{μ'} ≤ L ℓ_{μ+μ'}.

3. Case d = 0. Then Z_t is a 0-current and boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = 0 by definition. So M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = M_W(Z_t) ≤ L ℓ_μ ≤ L ℓ_μ + L ℓ_{μ'} ≤ L ℓ_{μ+μ'} by steps 1 and 2.

4. Case d = d' + 1.
(a) Second slicing. The current ∂X ∈ 𝒟_{d'+1}(U) has the admissible representation (μ', ξ') (hypothesis). Its boundary ∂∂X is 0 (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary) and has the admissible representation (0, 0) given by the zero measure and the zero field: the zero measure is finite on compact sets; every function is a.e. strongly measurable for the zero measure (aestronglyMeasurable_zero_measure); every a.e. statement holds for the zero measure (ae_zero); and ∂∂X(η) = 0 = ∫ 0 d0 (integral_zero_measure). Apply (SL) with k := d', U, T := ∂X, the representations (μ', ξ') of ∂X and (0, 0) of ∂∂X, f and L. It yields families A'_t ∈ 𝒟_{d'+1}(U), B'_t ∈ 𝒟_{d'}(U) with A'_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' = B_t(η) for every test form η, B'_t(ζ) = ∫_{f<t} 0 d0 = 0 for every ζ, and M_W(∂A'_t − B'_t) ≤ L ℓ_{μ'}. Currents are determined by their values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so A'_t = B_t and B'_t = 0; hence ∂A'_t − B'_t = ∂B_t − 0 = ∂B_t and M_W(∂B_t) ≤ L ℓ_{μ'}.
(b) Boundary of the slice. The boundary is additive: (S − T).boundary(ζ) = (S − T)(dζ) = S(dζ) − T(dζ) = ∂S(ζ) − ∂T(ζ). Hence ∂Z_t = ∂∂A_t − ∂B_t = 0 − ∂B_t, using ∂∂A_t = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary).
(c) For every current S ∈ 𝒟_m(U) and every set W, M_W(0 − S) ≤ M_W(S). Indeed, if ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) is admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x), then so is −ω (tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω by tsupport_neg, and covectorEuclideanNorm(−α) = covectorEuclideanNorm(α) by SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg), and (0 − S)(ω) = −S(ω) = S(−ω) by linearity (map_neg). Hence ofReal((0 − S)(ω)) = ofReal(S(−ω)) ≤ M_W(S) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), and taking the supremum over ω gives the claim.
(d) Therefore boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = M_W(∂Z_t) = M_W(0 − ∂B_t) ≤ M_W(∂B_t) ≤ L ℓ_{μ'}, and M_W(Z_t) + boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) ≤ L ℓ_μ + L ℓ_{μ'} ≤ L ℓ_{μ+μ'} by steps 1, 4(a)–(c) and 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: (SL) for X with (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') gives A_t, B_t with the integral formulas and M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L ℓ_μ.
In [0, ∞], liminf u + liminf v ≤ liminf (u + v), so L ℓ_μ + L ℓ_{μ'} ≤ L ℓ_{μ+μ'}.
If d = 0, boundaryMassOn is 0 and the bound follows.
If d = d' + 1, (SL) for ∂X with (μ', ξ') and the zero representation of ∂∂X = 0 identifies its first family with B_t and its second with 0, giving M_W(∂B_t) ≤ L ℓ_{μ'}.
∂(∂A_t − B_t) = 0 − ∂B_t and M_W(0 − S) ≤ M_W(S) bound boundaryMassOn by L ℓ_{μ'}; add the two bounds.
